happy to help! in terms of vr, be aware of a potential pitfall there. on the gaming systems that have a display output wired to the discrete gpu, its typically the hdmi output, because the initial wave of vr headsets used hdmi. some still do. however, the new oculus rift s switched over to displayport. displayport video output can be achieved from a usb-c port that supports video output by using a usb-c to displayport dongle. however, on every dell system im aware of that has a usb-c port that supports video output, the usb-c ports video interface is wired to the intel gpu. the only exceptions i know of are the precision 7000 series models from the xx20 onward, which have a bios option that allows you to choose which gpu controls the display outputs. they achieve that with a more complex and expensive motherboard design, but i havent seen that implemented elsewhere. so if youre trying for vr, you might have to give some thought to which vr headset you want to use, because if you have a system where only the hdmi output is wired to the discrete gpu, then you cant use a displayport-based vr headset. there are displayport to hdmi adapters, but they dont work in that direction. they can only convert a displayport source to an hdmi signal, not the other way around. theres also a new standard called virtuallink that is backed by all major vr headset and gpu manufacturers that is basically a new way to configure a usb-c interface to carry enough power, video, and data to run an entire vr headset from a single cable. its expected to be used on future vr headsets. i may be wrong here, but i dont think it will be possible to retrofit virtuallink support to existing systems because virtuallink basically involves running usb 3.0 traffic over pins on the usb-c connector that the current spec reserves for usb 2.0 (in order to increase available video bandwidth by reconfiguring the typical usb 3.0 pins for video). that said, i dont know of any virtuallink headsets on the market yet either, and i would expect that they would include some sort of breakout box that would separate that link into power, usb 3.0 data, and video so that those headset can be used from non-virtuallink systems, but even if those existed, they would need a displayport signal from the host system rather than hdmi, because again usb-c uses displayport for video. unfortunately, as i said earlier, finding a system that has a usb-c or displayport connector wired to the discrete gpu might be tricky at the moment. this will probably change on gaming systems going forward, but obviously that doesnt help if youre trying to buy a system today.
